result.summary: This PR reworks the log macro implementation to let LogTrace/LogDebug/LogInfo/LogWarning/LogError macros optionally accept a context/source object instead of only a bare category constant. The context object can carry a custom logger instance and a custom Format() hook, allowing subsystems (wallet, kernel) to attach metadata like wallet names or route messages to a non-global logger. It is fully backwards compatible: existing call sites are unaffected, and the PR is now largely limited to the macro/header rewrite plus tests and documentation, with the previously included wallet and kernel consumer code split into followup PRs (#30342, #30343).
result.problem: libbitcoinkernel applications currently can only log to one implicit global logger, and wallet code uses a bespoke WalletLogPrintf() wrapper that lacks severity levels and forces info-level logging. This PR is meant to let kernel consumers control where output goes and let wallet/index code use the standard macros while attaching subsystem-specific context, addressed for maintainers wanting to remove global-state dependencies from the kernel library and for wallet code needing structured logging.

open_concerns: ajtowns holds a Concept NACK: the new API adds complexity, more call-site verbosity, and multiple-logger support that he considers a design error for libbitcoinkernel; he sees no actual benefit demonstrated by real consumers.

hodlinator and l0rinc have raised numerous implementation-level concerns (naming, macro hygiene, avoiding accidental interfaces, commit granularity) across many rounds; most individually resolved via pushes but the PR keeps evolving in response to new reviews.
No maintainer consensus that the underlying design (context/source objects, multiple logger instances) is wanted.
resolved_concerns: hodlinator's original NACK over LogInfo accepting categories was addressed by reinstating #28318 restrictions (categories still forbidden for Info/Warning/Error).
Numerous style/test nits from l0rinc and hodlinator were implemented in later pushes (constexpr arrays, ReadDebugLogLines reuse, removing superfluous lambdas/inheritance).
Concerns about output-format regressions (missing [net:info] style prefixes) were fixed by restoring prior formatting behavior.

A maintainer (ajtowns) disputes that the underlying design solves a real problem, and no consumer of the new API has landed yet after nearly two years, which tempers its urgency despite the leverage argument for unblocking dependent work.

result.card: This long-running PR (open since Jan 2024, 36 force-pushes) reworks Bitcoin Core's logging macros so LogDebug/LogInfo/LogError etc. can accept an optional context object, letting subsystems attach metadata (e.g. wallet name) or direct output to a non-global logger. It is backwards compatible and mainly serves as a dependency for followup PRs #30342 (kernel multi-logger support) and #30343 (replacing WalletLogPrintf), neither of which has merged. The strongest evidence of its importance is that leverage for those dependents, but the core problem it solves is disputed: maintainer ajtowns maintains a long-standing Concept NACK arguing the added complexity has no demonstrated benefit, and no consumer of the new API has actually merged. Reviewability is Ready since CI is green and the design has stabilized after extensive iterative feedback from hodlinator and l0rinc, but Agreement is Disputed given the unresolved maintainer-level objection despite the author's extensive engagement.
